title: Sell Mineral Rights in Antelope, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Antelope, MT
metaDescription: Mineral rights near Antelope in Sheridan County, MT? A retired E&P engineer explains why this far-northeast corner sits on the thin edge of the Bakken.
heroLead: Antelope sits about as far from the productive core of the Bakken as this state gets, and I'd rather tell you that plainly than let a slick offer imply otherwise.
intro: Sheridan County occupies Montana's northeast corner, wheat and cattle country running right up against the Saskatchewan line, and Antelope is a small community inside that county rather than an incorporated town with its own courthouse. Your title work for anything here runs through Plentywood, the county seat, which is where I'd start any real title check before quoting a number.

sections.heading: Flank Geology, Honestly Stated
paragraphs: The Bakken and underlying Three Forks formations do extend under Sheridan County, but this is the far western edge of the play, well removed from the Elm Coulee-style pay thickness that made Richland County productive. Wells here, where they exist at all, tend to be thinner, more marginal, and less consistently economic than anything closer to the North Dakota line. I don't say that to talk your interest down, I say it because an honest starting point saves you from comparing your offer to a core-county number that was never going to apply.

sections.heading: What Ownership Usually Looks Like Here
paragraphs: Most mineral interests I see out of this part of Sheridan County trace back to original homestead patents from the early 1900s, often severed from the surface at some point and passed down through several generations of the same farming or ranching family. Fractional interests are common, split among heirs who may not even live in Montana anymore. If that describes your situation, confirming exactly what percentage you hold, and against which specific tract, is the real first step before any value discussion makes sense.

sections.heading: What I'd Actually Look At
paragraphs: For a tract in this area, I check whether there's any current leasing activity nearby, what the recorded chain of title shows for your net revenue interest, and whether any historical wells on or near the tract are still producing or have been plugged. Given how far this sits from the play's core, undeveloped or lightly developed interests here are a longer-term hold-or-sell decision than in the eastern Bakken counties, and I'll walk through that honestly rather than push a number that assumes activity that isn't there.

faqs.question: Is Antelope, MT inside the productive Bakken core?
faqs.answer: No. Sheridan County sits on the far western flank of the play, well removed from the thicker, more productive Elm Coulee-area pay in Richland County. Activity and economics here have historically been thinner and more marginal.

faqs.question: Where do I check the title on minerals near Antelope?
faqs.answer: Sheridan County Clerk and Recorder in Plentywood handles the recorded chain of title for anything in this part of the county, including Antelope.

faqs.question: My family's mineral interest near Antelope has never produced. Is it worth selling?
faqs.answer: It can still have value, but it's a more speculative, longer-horizon value given the county's distance from the play's core. I'd give you an honest range rather than imply near-term drilling interest that isn't there.
